title: Local ind-etale extensions of a DVR preserve its uniformizer
statement: Let $U$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_U=(\pi)$ and fraction field $F$. Let $T$ be a nonzero commutative local ring and let $U\to T$ be a local ind-etale map [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]; local means that the maximal ideal of $T$ pulls back to $\mathfrak m_U$. No Noetherianity of $T$ is assumed. Then $U\to T$ is injective, $T$ is a discrete valuation ring, $\mathfrak m_T=\pi T$, and the induced fraction-field extension $\operatorname{Frac}(T)/F$ is separable algebraic [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. More generally, let $D$ be any commutative $U$-algebra, let $p$ be a prime of $D$, and let $q$ be a prime of $T\otimes_U D$ whose contraction is $p$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. If $D_p$ is a discrete valuation ring, then $(T\otimes_U D)_q$ is a discrete valuation ring and the canonical local map $D_p\to(T\otimes_U D)_q$ is injective and carries a uniformizer to a uniformizer; equivalently $p(T\otimes_U D)_q=q(T\otimes_U D)_q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

proof.text: We prove the local assertion in the following notation, which also accommodates base change. Let $R$ be a DVR with uniformizer $t$, let $E=\varinjlim_i B_i$ be a small filtered colimit of etale $R$-algebras, and let $n\subset E$ contract to $\mathfrak m_R$. Put $S=E_n$, $n_i=n\cap B_i$, and $L_i=(B_i)_{n_i}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-localization-at-prime], $S=\varinjlim_i L_i$ with the displayed fraction transition maps. They and the legs into $S$ are local: $a/s$ is in the target maximal ideal exactly when $a$ is in the contracted prime. By [lem-sbc-etale-trait-stalk], the stalk of $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ at $n_i$ is a domain DVR, the structural map from $R$ is injective, and its maximal ideal is generated by $t$. The canonical identification with $L_i$ in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] preserves structural images. Thus each $L_i$ has all these properties.

source.place: Tag 0AP2 (lemma-Dedekind-etale-extension), local-ring assertion; algebra.tex Tag 037D (lemma-colimit-normal-ring), localized colimit in its proof.

proof.text: Every transition $L_i\to L_j$ is injective. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] writes a nonzero $a\in L_i$ as $ut^e$ with $u$ a unit. Its image is the product of a unit and $t^e\ne0$ in the domain $L_j$, so cannot vanish. The colimit legs $L_i\to S$ are injective too: if $a\in L_i$ has zero image, [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] provides arrows $i\to k$ carrying $a$ and $0$ to equal elements of $L_k$. The image of $0$ along either arrow is $0$, so the injectivity of the arrow carrying $a$ gives $a=0$. Any two elements of $S$ lift to a common $L_i$; their product can be zero only if one lift is zero, since the leg is injective. Hence $S$ is a domain. Choosing any stage also proves $R\to S$ injective.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), final assertion; Tags 00D6 and 00D7 (lemma-directed-colimit, lemma-zero-directed-limit).

proof.text: Every nonzero $x\in S$ comes from a nonzero element of some $L_i$, so [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] gives $x=ut^e$ with $u\in S^\times$ and $e\ge0$. Here $t$ is nonzero by injectivity and belongs to the maximal ideal of $S$ by contraction. The exponent is unique: from $ut^e=vt^f\ne0$, if $e<f$, cancellation in the domain gives $u=vt^{f-e}$, impossible since the right side lies in the maximal ideal and $u$ is a unit. The case $f<e$ is symmetric. For every nonzero ideal $J\subset S$, take an element with least exponent $e$ among its nonzero elements. It gives $t^e\in J$; every other nonzero element $vt^f$ has $f\ge e$ and equals $t^e(vt^{f-e})$. Thus $J=(t^e)$; the zero ideal is principal too. Therefore $S$ is a local principal ideal domain and is not a field, exactly a DVR as in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Its maximal ideal is $(t)$: its nonzero elements have positive exponent by [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion], whereas exponent zero gives a unit.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), unit-times-power description; elementary least-exponent argument, written by Q79.

proof.text: For the fraction-field assertion, apply [lem-trf-ind-etale-residue-separable] to $R\to E$ and the prime $Q\subset E$ pulled back from $(0)\subset S=E_n$. Its contraction to $R$ is $(0)$ since $R\to S$ is injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], $\kappa_E(Q)\cong\kappa_S((0))$ compatibly with $R$. For a domain localization at zero is its fraction field, by the fraction definition [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Thus $\kappa_R((0))=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ and $\kappa_E(Q)=\operatorname{Frac}(S)$ under the canonical maps. The cited separability assertion proves that $\operatorname{Frac}(S)/\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ is separable algebraic.

Apply Steps 1--4 with $R=U$, $E=T$, $n=\mathfrak m_T$, using the etale presentation in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. A local ring is canonically its localization at its maximal ideal: denominators outside it are units by [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion], and the inverse sends $a/s$ to $as^{-1}$. This identifies $S$ with $T$ over $U$. It proves injectivity, the DVR assertion, $\mathfrak m_T=\pi T$, and separable algebraicity on fraction fields. No Noetherian hypothesis on $T$ entered the argument; principality of every ideal was proved in Step 3.

source.place: Agent extension of Tags 0AP2 and 0AH1 (lemma-filtered-colimit-etale-noetherian-fibres), avoiding a Noetherianity assumption on T.

proof.text: For the last clause put $A=T\otimes_U D$, $R=D_p$, and $E=T\otimes_U D_p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], $E$ is ind-etale over $R$, hence has a small filtered etale presentation. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base], interchanging tensor factors, $A\to E$ is localization at the images of $D\setminus p$; its fraction formula is $t\otimes(d/s)\mapsto(t\otimes d)/(1\otimes s)$. This module identification respects multiplication and $1$ on pure tensors, hence is a ring identification. Because $q\cap D=p$, these denominators avoid $q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], $q$ extends to a prime $r\subset E$ and $A_q\cong E_r$ canonically over $D$. The contraction of $r$ to $R$ is $pR$: a fraction $d/s$ belongs to $r$ exactly when $d\in p$. Steps 1--3 applied to this $R,E,r$ now give that $A_q$ is a DVR, the canonical local map $D_p\to A_q$ is injective, and its maximal ideal is generated by the image of any uniformizer of $D_p$. Since $pD_p$ is its source maximal ideal, this is precisely $pA_q=qA_q$.
